TITLE: LuxQuanta Wins Europe’s Top Startup Award at GITEX Europe 2025

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The ICFO spin-off company LuxQuanta wins the Startup Award at GITEX Europe, the largest and most collaborative tech event in Europe. LuxQuanta, a spin-off company founded by the BIST Community centre ICFO, has been selected as the winner of the GITEX Supernova All-Stars start-up award. The GITEX Supernova All-Stars is fast becoming a benchmark event for identifying not only Europe’s most promising startups and business models, but also serving as a launchpad for the continent’s next wave of unicorn start-ups. Hosted in Berlin, this trade show is dedicated to bridging and uniting big tech, startups, and SMBs from across Europe and beyond, forging powerful relationships that unlock collaborative opportunities and connections that aim to spark innovation. After being selected as a semi-finalist from a pool of more than 700 companies, Vanesa Díaz, CEO of LuxQuanta, was given the opportunity to deliver a 2-minute pitch where over 100 startups competed for a spot in the grand finale. As one of the finalists and in front of a jury of top-tier angel investors and deep-tech experts who carefully assessed the quality of each pitch and the strength of the underlying business models, Díaz summarized the company’s journey once again, in just two minutes. She highlighted LuxQuanta’s mission to secure digital communications, the recent launch of the second generation of NOVA LQ, the challenges ahead, and most importantly, the incredible team that pushes this technology forward. Winning this prize “is a true testament to all the hard work we have put into this project. It’s been four years of relentless effort, resilience, and enthusiasm.” Díaz emphasized as she expressed the company’s commitment to being a reliable provider of cybersecurity solutions in the quantum era. The recognition at GITEX Europe positions LuxQuanta on the international stage, attracting attention from investors, industry leaders and potential collaborators. This is a critical step in supporting the company’s mission to bring Quantum-Safe Security to businesses and institutions worldwide. LuxQuanta is ICFO’s tenth spin-off company. Constituted in May 2021, it focuses on the development and commercialization of quantum key distribution systems (QKD) for cryptography, including continuous variable quantum key distribution systems, to implement an extra layer of security services for companies and network infrastructures both in the public and private sectors. As Silvia Carrasco, Vice Director of Innovation, Sponsored Research and Public Engagement at ICFO, concludes, “We feel deeply proud and inspired to see LuxQuanta receive this well-deserved recognition. It reflects the company’s technological excellence and the remarkable team behind it. Seeing their work acknowledged on the global stage reinforces the impact of science-driven entrepreneurship.” Learn more: LuxQuanta GITEX Europe Source: ICFO news

TITLE: Luis Serrano and Katherine Villa receive Catalonia’s National Research Awards

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Two members of the BIST Community have been honoured with 2025 National Research Awards (Premis Nacionals de Recerca), presented by the Government of Catalonia and the Catalan Foundation for Research and Innovation (FCRI). Luis Serrano, Director of the CRG, has received the National Research Award, Catalonia’s highest scientific distinction, and Katherine Villa, Group Leader at ICIQ, was recognised with the award for Young Talent. These awards, this year in their 36th edition, promote the social recognition of science, highlighting excellence in research, patronage, entrepreneurship and communication, as well as the organisations that drive knowledge transfer and the creation of science-based companies. The National Research Award, the highest scientific honour in Catalonia, honours researchers whose work has had significant international impact. Luis Serrano, ICREA Professor and director of the BIST Community centre CRG, has been awarded this year in recognition of his pioneering contributions to systems biology and protein design. The National Research Award for Young Talent recognises the scientific excellence and career of young researchers who have made a significant contribution to the advancement of science. ICREA Professor and Group Leader at ICIQ, Katherine Villa, has received the award this year for her work on photocatalytic materials and photoactive micromotors. Luis Serrano In a speech during the awards ceremony, which took place on February 20th in Barcelona, Serrano pointed out that “Science is never an individual achievement. Behind any discovery there are teams, institutions and an ecosystem that makes it possible. This prize recognises a trajectory, but it also recognises a system.” The distinction comes at a symbolic moment for Serrano. After fifteen years at the helm of the CRG, he will step down as Director later this year. Luis Serrano’s career has been defined by a drive to uncover the physical rules that govern living systems, and to use that knowledge to design new ones. Trained in biochemistry and cellular biology in Madrid, Cambridge and Heidelberg, he became internationally known for his work on the thermodynamic principles of protein folding, helping explain how a protein’s structure determines its function. One of his most widely adopted contributions is FoldX, a computational tool used by researchers and pharmaceutical companies worldwide to predict the effects of mutations and guide rational protein design. “FoldX began almost as an intellectual exercise,” Serrano reflects. “We wanted to understand how small changes in a protein’s sequence affect its stability. Today, that same framework is helping to design enzymes, understand disease mutations and accelerate drug development. It’s a reminder that rigorous basic science can travel much further than you initially imagine.” Beyond individual molecules, his work expanded into quantitative models of gene regulation and signalling networks, helping bridge molecular biology with engineering approaches that underpin modern synthetic biology. If he had to summarise his career in one idea, Serrano told the audience, it would be this: “I’ve tried to be a builder of systems: biological systems, of course, but also human and institutional systems.” In his speech, Serrano also emphasised the strength of Catalonia’s research landscape. “For years we said we wanted to ‘play in the Champions League’ of European science,” he noted. “Today, we can say we are there. That is something to celebrate.” But celebration, he added, must be matched by ambition. “Being in the Champions League does not mean you relax. It means the challenge is greater. TITLE: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 in Japan: JPY 362,000 Monthly Stipend, Airfare and 120 Awards per Open-Call Round

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
The Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS) Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan – Standard Program offers outstanding early-career researchers from around the world an opportunity to spend 12 to 24 months conducting collaborative research at universities and eligible research institutions in Japan. The fellowship is one of Japan’s major international postdoctoral research programmes and is open across an exceptionally broad range of academic disciplines, including the humanities, social sciences and natural sciences. Successful Fellows work under the guidance of an eligible Japanese host researcher and join an established research environment in Japan while developing an international collaborative research project. Financial support under the Standard Program includes a JPY 362,000 monthly maintenance allowance, a round-trip international air ticket under JSPS rules, a JPY 200,000 settling-in allowance, overseas travel insurance and access to a separate Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research for eligible collaborative research expenses. For FY2027, JSPS has scheduled two open-call recruitment rounds, with approximately 120 Fellowships planned in each round. The first round deadline was 28 August 2026 at 5:00 PM Japan Standard Time, while the second-round deadline is 23 April 2027 at 5:00 PM JST. This deadline information is important because some third-party posts circulating online state that the application deadline is 15 November 2026. That date does not appear in the official JSPS FY2027 Standard Program open-call schedule. Applicants using an overseas nominating authority may face separate deadlines set by that nominating organization, but those deadlines vary by country and should not be presented as the universal JSPS deadline. The official FY2027 Standard Program should therefore be understood as a host-based, highly competitive international postdoctoral fellowship, not a direct individual online application in which a researcher simply submits independently to JSPS. Official programme information: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan; JSPS International Fellowships for Research in Japan 2026 About the JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan The Japan Society for the Promotion of Science operates several international fellowship programmes designed for researchers at different stages of their careers. These include programmes for: Pre-doctoral researchers Postdoctoral researchers Early-career researchers Experienced international researchers Short-term research visitors The Standard Program, however, is specifically designed to give young overseas postdoctoral researchers an opportunity to conduct collaborative research with leading research groups at Japanese universities and other eligible research institutions. The programme emphasizes genuine research collaboration rather than simply providing a researcher with funding to work independently. Before an application is submitted, the overseas candidate and Japanese host researcher are expected to: Establish contact Develop a concrete research plan Agree on the proposed collaboration Identify an appropriate host institution Demonstrate how the collaboration will advance the proposed research These factors are explicitly considered during the JSPS selection process. Fellowship Duration The Standard Program runs for: 12 to 24 months. This gives successful Fellows enough time to become meaningfully integrated into the host research environment rather than undertaking only a short academic visit. Depending on the project, a Fellow may therefore spend: One year 18 months Two years conducting research in Japan. The precise tenure is proposed through the application and should match the needs of the research collaboration. FY2027 Number of Fellowships The official FY2027 open-call schedule lists approximately: 120 Fellowship awards in the first recruitment round and another: 120 Fellowship awards in the second recruitment round. Therefore, the frequently advertised figure of “120 awards” is broadly correct for each FY2027 open-call recruitment round, rather than necessarily representing the total number of all Standard Program awards through every application route. JSPS also receives Standard Program applications through overseas nominating authorities in selected countries and organisations. FY2027 First Recruitment Round

TITLE: Four BIST Community Researchers receive ERC Proof of Concept Grants

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
Dr. Irene Marco-Rius, Dr. Nicolò Accanto, and Dr. Benedetta Bolognesi (IBEC), and Dr. Klaas-Jan Tielrooij (ICN2) have each received a prestigious ERC Proof of Concept grant. The researchers will receive €150 000 each, to explore the commercial and social potential of their existing research. ERC Proof of Concept Grant Recipients from the BIST Community: (left to right) Irene Marco-Rius, Nicolò Accanto, Benedetta Bolognesi, Klaas-Jan Tielrooij. Benedetta Bolognesi, Irene Marco-Rius and Nicolò Accanto, group leaders at the Institute for Bioengineering of Catalonia (IBEC), and Klaas-Jan Tielrooij, group leader at the Catalan Institute of Nanoscience and Nanotechnology (ICN2), have each been awarded an ERC Proof of Concept (PoC) Grant. These prestigious grants are awarded by the European Research Council (ERC) to explore the commercial and social potential of research projects that have previously received ERC funding. Applicants use this funding to verify the practical feasibility of scientific concepts, explore business opportunities, or prepare patent applications. In total, 300 Proof of Concept projects have been funded in 2025 under the €45 million Horizon Europe programme. In this current call, these four researchers from the BIST Community will aim to develop effective treatments for diseases such as Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s, to facilitate advances towards personalised medicine, to unlock new possibilities for neuroscience laboratories, and to develop a new measurement method using graphene-based detectors. AMALIA: A scalable platform to accelerate the discovery of small anti-amyloid molecules Led by Benedetta Bolognesi, leader of the Protein Phase Transitions in Health and Disease group at IBEC, the AMALIA project addresses one of today’s greatest biomedical challenges: developing effective treatments for diseases such as Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s, which are driven by the formation of protein aggregates known as amyloids. Despite decades of research, the initial events that trigger this aggregation process are still extremely difficult to study, and there are currently no scalable assays capable of systematically evaluating amyloid nucleation. AMALIA proposes a dual, massively scalable screening platform combining two complementary assays. The first is aimed at identifying molecules that can stabilise the native structure of globular proteins, thereby preventing their aggregation. The second is designed to detect inhibitors of amyloid nucleation in both folded and intrinsically disordered proteins. As part of this proof of concept based on the Glam-MAP project, the team will miniaturise and automate these assays to optimise them and carry out multi-target pilot screening. This will demonstrate their ability to operate in parallel on different amyloid targets. AMALIA is conceived as a platform technology that goes beyond a single project or target: a tool that eliminates the need for purified proteins and enables parallel discovery campaigns on multiple amyloid targets. This approach offers unprecedented speed and scalability. The aim of AMALIA is to transform the search for anti-amyloid therapies and contribute to reducing the enormous health and economic impact of these diseases. “I’m thrilled that with AMALIA we are bringing the speed and scalability of platform technologies to amyloid drug discovery – building a pipeline designed not to deliver just one drug, but to enable multiple therapeutic programs in parallel.”, says Bolognesi. CAMP: A magnetic resonance platform for high-sensitivity metabolic analysis in rare diseases Led by Irene Marco-Rius, who heads the Molecular Imaging for Precision Medicine group at IBEC, the CAMP project seeks to commercialise technology combining microfluidics and hyperpolarised magnetic resonance. This development is based on technology generated by the LIFETIME project, which focuses on paediatric liver cancer models. CAMP will enable the simultaneous analysis of up to 30 samples by integrating microfluidic chips with magnetic resonance technology, significantly increasing sensitivity. This combination reduces the number of cells required per sample by over 50%,

International historians and postdoctoral researchers specializing in twentieth-century German, European, or Eastern European history have an opportunity to spend two months conducting independent research in Germany through the Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027 at the Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam (Leibniz-Zentrum für Zeithistorische Forschung Potsdam – ZZF). For the 2027 fellowship cycle, ZZF is inviting applications for two Leibniz Summer Fellowships focused on German and/or European, including Eastern European, History in the Twentieth Century. The program is specifically intended for international scholars who already hold a doctoral degree and are residing outside Germany when they apply. Successful fellows will spend two consecutive months in Berlin or Potsdam between April and October 2027. Each fellow will receive a monthly grant of €3,000, meaning that a two-month fellowship provides €6,000 in total grant support. The funding is intended to cover the fellow’s living costs, travel and appropriate insurance during the fellowship period. The application deadline is November 30, 2026. About the Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027 The Leibniz Summer Fellowship is a research residency offered by the Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam for established international scholars working in areas relevant to twentieth-century German and European history. The program combines two important elements: independent scholarly research and active participation in the intellectual life of ZZF. Rather than requiring fellows to work on a predetermined institutional project, ZZF allows successful applicants to continue research based on their own scholarly interests. Preference, however, is given to proposals that connect with one or more of the Centre’s existing research departments. This approach makes the fellowship particularly attractive to postdoctoral historians who already have a developed research agenda and would benefit from access to German academic networks, historical resources and interaction with specialists working on related themes. Host Institution: Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam The Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam, commonly known as ZZF, is a major German research institute specializing in twentieth-century contemporary history and its connections with the present. Its work places particular emphasis on German and European social history after 1945 while situating those developments within broader international contexts. In addition to fundamental historical research, ZZF is involved in research infrastructure, digital knowledge transfer and cooperation with universities and research institutions in Germany and abroad. ZZF is a member of the Leibniz Association, one of Germany’s major networks of non-university research institutions. The Centre has held Leibniz Association membership since 2009 and receives institutional support from both federal and state-level public funding. The institute also has an extensive international academic orientation, including cooperation with universities and research organizations as well as a visiting-researcher program. These connections help make the fellowship more than simply a short period of individual archival or library research. Two Fellowships Available for 2027 ZZF has announced two positions under the 2027 Leibniz Summer Fellowship program. The thematic field is: German and/or European, including Eastern European, History in the Twentieth Century This is broad enough to accommodate scholars working across multiple subfields of contemporary history, provided that their research has a substantive connection to German or European twentieth-century history. The opportunity is intended for international postdoctoral researchers rather than doctoral students or applicants who have not yet completed their doctorate. TITLE: Carnegie African Diaspora Fellowship Program Announces Partnership with the Association of African Universities and Selects New Fellows

OPPORTUNITY TEXT:
NEW YORK, and ACCRA, GHANA June 27, 2022 – The Carnegie African Diaspora Fellowship Program (CADFP) announces the award of 56 fellowships to individuals and institutions to take part in joint academic projects with resident institutions in Africa. To date, the CADFP has funded 584 fellowships for African-born scholars from the United States and Canada to collaborate with over 203 institutions of higher learning in Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Senegal, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda in the areas of collaborative research, curriculum co-development and graduate student teaching and mentoring. Nearly a decade since the launch of CADFP, the Carnegie Corporation of New York and the Institute of International Education (IIE) continue working with partners, Fellows and Hosts to deepen and strengthen the highly successful CADFP model. In addition to an Advisory Council of prominent African academics, the program has established a new partnership with the Association of African Universities (AAU), a Pan-African higher education institution with a membership of over 400 universities, and focused on higher education development and policy. With the diaspora as a strategic priority, AAU engages governments across Africa on various issues, including advocacy for incremental investments in the higher education sector. The Association also collaborates with key stakeholders to support human capacity development, academic scholarship and innovative research, ultimately aimed at propelling the higher education sector to contribute more effectively to the continent’s transformation and development agenda. In April of this year, AAU, IIE, and CCNY convened the Advisory Council to select the 56 awardees and hosted a highly successful CADFP Stakeholder Forum in Accra, Ghana. The forum brought together country-level participants including Ghana’s former Minister of Education, Hon. Prof. Jane Naana Opoku Agyemang; the Director of Tertiary Education, Ministry of Education, Dr. Eric Nkansah; the Director of Diaspora Affairs, Office of the President, Ghana, Mr. Akwasi Ababio; as well as international development partners, host institutions, fellows and alumni of the CADFP. CADFP fellows traveling to Africa will collaborate with academics at their host institutions on a variety of projects, ultimately aimed at working synergistically to improve the quality of African higher education. A full list of the most current projects can be found here. Through these initiatives, CADFP aims to find solutions to some of the most pressing challenges facing Africa and the world. How the Projects and Fellowships Work: Fellowships match host universities with African-born scholars from Canada or the United States, individually or in groups, and cover the expenses for project visits of up to three months. All scholar and project proposals are evaluated by an independent review committee and must be approved by the Advisory Council. Public and private higher education institutions in Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda, along with member universities or affiliates of the African Research Universities Alliance including Addis Ababa University, Cheikh Anta Diop University, University of Mauritius, and University of Rwanda are invited to submit a project request to host a scholar for 21 to 90 days. Prospective hosts are eligible but not required to name a proposed scholar in their request. The Association of African Universities (AAU) celebrates a proud and historic moment for African higher education. Two of our most distinguished leaders have ascended to high office within the Association of Commonwealth Universities (ACU), placing the continent’s voice at the very heart of one of the world’s oldest and most influential university networks. This dual achievement highlights the global recognition of the leadership cultivated within the AAU’s membership and underscores our collective commitment to shaping the future of higher education worldwide. Professor Kenneth Matengu, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Namibia and the elected President of the AAU Governing Board, was elected to the ACU Council in July 2025. He currently serves as a Council Member and Trustee, representing Constituency III – comprising East, West and Southern Africa – for a three-year term from 01 August 2025 to 31 July 2028. In a related recent and prestigious development, Professor Nana Aba Appiah Amfo, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ghana and the AAU Ambassador for Gender Equity & Social Inclusion, has been elected as the Chair of the ACU Council. She will provide strategic leadership for an initial two-year term, effective 1 January 2026, after having served as a valuable member of the Council since August 2024. A Powerful Convergence of Governance and Advocacy These appointments are not just personal accolades; they represent a strategic alignment of the AAU’s core missions on a global platform. Prof. Kenneth Matengu brings to the ACU Council his dynamic vision as the youngest-ever AAU President and his deep commitment to pan-African collaboration. His leadership is instrumental in driving initiatives that strengthen universities across the continent. Upon his election, Prof. Matengu stated his focus would be on “supporting postgraduate education and research, especially as Africa works to produce the next generation of doctoral graduates needed to realise our continent’s vision for the future.” Prof. Nana Aba Appiah Amfo ascends to the ACU Chairmanship as a proven leader and a powerful voice for the values the AAU champions. Her role as our Ambassador for Gender Equity & Social Inclusion is a testament to her lifelong commitment to these principles. In her new role, she aims to “strengthen collaboration, advance equity and inclusion and ensure that higher education continues to serve as a powerful force for sustainable development and societal transformation.” A Statement from the AAU Secretariat The AAU community is immensely proud of Professors Matengu and Amfo. Their elections are a resounding endorsement of African leadership and the relevance of our continental agenda. To have our Board President on the ACU Council and our Ambassador for Gender Equity assuming its Chairmanship creates a unique and powerful synergy. It ensures that Africa’s priorities, from building research capacity to championing inclusive education, will be advocated for at the highest level of Commonwealth dialogue. This is a victory for every AAU member institution. Celebrating Our Members, Elevating Our Continent As the apex organisation for higher education in Africa, the AAU exists to connect, support, and celebrate the achievements of its members. The global recognition of Prof. Matengu and Prof. Amfo is a direct reflection of the excellence nurtured within the University of Namibia and the University of Ghana. We extend our heartfelt congratulations to these esteemed institutions for fostering such exemplary leadership. We look forward to the strengthened partnership between the AAU and the ACU under this joint leadership. Their roles promise to foster greater collaboration, drive innovative solutions to shared challenges, and ensure that African universities continue to play a pivotal role in the global knowledge ecosystem. Professor Kenneth Matengu and Professor Nana Aba Appiah Amfo have attained key global leadership roles on the Association of Commonwealth Universities (ACU) Council. Professor Matengu serves as a Council Member and Trustee representing Constituency III for a three-year term from 01 August 2025 to 31 July 2028. Professor Amfo serves as the Chair of the ACU Council for an initial two-year term effective 1 January 2026.
